clue.text: Head in old coin

definitions.meaning: the top of the head, as in a hat fitting at that spot
a pre-decimal British coin worth five shillings

explanation.surface: A monarch's head stamped on an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a portrait on a coin, and both halves are the answer. A crown was a British coin worth five shillings, a quarter of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the crown is the top part of the head.

clue.text: Selfish driver who may sound like a bore?

definitions.text: Selfish driver who may sound like a bore?

parts.note: a motorist who takes more than a fair share of the lane

parts.words: who may sound like a bore?
parts.note: not a tedious talker: a bore sounds like a boar, the wild pig, which is a kind of swine

explanation.surface: A tedious motorist who drones on behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: A hog is a pig, like a boar, so the selfish motorist is a road hog, and a boar is what 'bore' sounds like; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a road hog is a motorist who hogs the road, driving selfishly.

clue.text: Person flogging fish is an impudent type

parts.note: the snapper is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A cheeky fishmonger shouting his wares at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging fish' reads as selling fish at a stall; here flogging means whipping, and the fish is a separate item.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a whippersnapper is a young and presumptuous person.

clue.text: Precious metal consumed stone

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed a valuable piece of metal and a pebble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious metal' could be gold (AU) or silver (AG); only silver's symbol fits here.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: agate is a banded semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Leave wife and split costs

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for one's wife

explanation.surface: A divorce: walking out on your wife and dividing the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch for wife comes from Cockney 'my old Dutch' (short for duchess), a London working-class term of affection for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to go Dutch is to have each person pay their own share.

clue.text: Fairy tale featuring Jack's beanstalk, perhaps?

definitions.text: Fairy tale featuring Jack's beanstalk, perhaps?

parts.note: read as a children's story, but also any far-fetched, untrue account
the beanstalk grows up to the clouds, so this is a story about something of great height

explanation.surface: Jack and the Beanstalk introduced as a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and the Beanstalk is literally a story about something tall, and it is also far-fetched, which is what a tall story is.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a tall story is an exaggerated, hard-to-believe account, much like a fairy tale.

clue.text: Swallow feathers

definitions.meaning: the verb, as in gulping a pint in one go
the soft fine feathers of a bird, used to fill duvets

explanation.surface: A swallow's plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Swallow the bird, owning the feathers; it is the verb, as in downing a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses: to swallow quickly, and a bird's soft under-plumage.

clue.text: Living ingredients in a pudding?

definitions.meaning: the noun, a livelihood: the basic work that pays the bills
a traditional British baked dessert is named after its two main ingredients

explanation.surface: Wondering what live things might be in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Living is the noun, a livelihood, not the adjective. Bread and butter pudding is a British dessert of buttered bread baked in custard.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the work that earns one's basic income is one's bread and butter.

clue.text: TV show Israel broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter, so the letters are strewn about

explanation.surface: A television programme aired by Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast sits beside TV so naturally it reads as airing; it originally meant sowing seed by scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a programme told in instalments is one kind of TV show.

clue.text: Many staff and I go out of business

parts.note: a firm that folds goes out of business

explanation.surface: A worker and many colleagues losing their jobs as the firm closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many staff' looks like a single phrase about a big workforce; Many is the definition and staff starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly literary: 'many-fold' means numerous and varied.

clue.text: Drink spiked by king, more significant

indicators.note: a drink spiked by something has it slipped inside

explanation.surface: A royal slipping something into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiking a drink means adding something to it, which is exactly what a container does to the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bigger, in the sense of mattering more.

clue.text: Maestro, foremost of composers, I'll give you a lift!

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is its first

parts.note: 'Hop in!' is what a driver offering a lift says

explanation.surface: A driver cheerfully offering a great composer a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation is a spoken phrase to be replaced by another: someone offering a lift says 'Hop in!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Polish pianist-composer is one maestro.

clue.text: Where devil lives, I am Satan transformed

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: The Devil announcing himself in a new guise, with Hell as his home.
explanation.walkthrough: The devil is not Satan but the Tasmanian devil, a small fierce marsupial found only on that Australian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the island is the only wild home of the marsupial called the devil.

clue.text: Savage sharing decorative food

indicators.note: to savage is to maul, so the letters are torn about

explanation.surface: Fierce squabbling over a plate of decorative nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Savage looks like an adjective describing the sharing; it is the instruction to maul the letters of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: food added to a dish for decoration or flavour.

clue.text: Feeling at home with training

explanation.surface: Feeling comfortable with a home-study course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeling at home' reads as one phrase meaning comfortable; it splits after Feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hunch, known without reasoning.

clue.text: How medicine may be given, failing that partner

explanation.surface: A doctor's instructions: take the medicine, or have your partner give it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing that' is a whole phrase standing for one tiny word, the conjunction that offers an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: by mouth, the usual route for tablets and syrups.

clue.text: Glossy trap — something attractive

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine, a mag

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine as a lure for something appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Glossy looks like an adjective but is the noun for a magazine printed on shiny paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on attraction: literally it pulls iron, figuratively it draws people.

clue.text: Old clothes on — yes!

definitions.note: an exclamation of assent, used in speech as 'Agreed!'

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it round

explanation.surface: Agreeing to put on some old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes is a verb here, and 'on' means concerning, as in memo headers.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of assent, said as a hearty yes.

clue.text: Major English political party is anxious

parts.note: a major is a musical key
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: A big English party nervous before an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Major looks like 'big', describing the party; it is the musical key. The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: wound up tight with nerves, like a tuned string.

clue.text: Ensure relative remains shut up!

definitions.meaning: read literally: make sure your mother stays

explanation.surface: An order to make a relative stay put, and be quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read literally, retain plus mother. Mum meaning silent is British usage, as in the wartime slogan 'Be like Dad, keep Mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: mum means silent, so the phrase orders silence.

clue.text: Recognise when ready for mining work?

definitions.meaning: to spot someone in a crowd
a miner's tool drawn and in hand

explanation.surface: Spotting when the miners are about to start digging.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical, flagged by the question mark: with the pick out, the miner is ready to dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to single out and identify from among others.

clue.text: Lead in pencil I gather wrong — it's a form of carbon

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order
the lead, or leading letter, of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Someone correcting a belief that pencil lead is actually lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a true fact: pencil 'lead' is not lead at all but this carbon. Here 'Lead in' just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the soft grey crystalline carbon used in pencils.

clue.text: Meal right, pack sandwiches

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to put it between two layers

parts.note: a pack is a bunch, a group

explanation.surface: Planning a picnic: pack the sandwiches for the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwiches reads as food, fitting Meal; it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the late-morning meal blending breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Judicial punishment swift, say

definitions.meaning: British slang for time served in prison
the swift is one example of a feathered flier

explanation.surface: Calling for justice to be swift.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift looks like an adjective about fast justice; it is the creature. Bird for prison time is British slang, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' = time.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: British slang for a prison sentence, as in 'doing bird'.

clue.text: Currency in which yours truly invested, the first person from Asia

definitions.note: adjective phrase for the adjective YEMENI

indicators.note: together with 'invested', points to the currency as the outer part
money invested is put into something

parts.note: I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A letter-writer describing a currency they put money in, and the first person to do so from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Yemen is on the Arabian Peninsula, which is part of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: from one country in western Asia.

clue.text: Two-hour race for some, relative jogged round though

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: though shortened by dropping its last three letters UGH, the informal spelling tho'

explanation.surface: Elite runners finish a marathon in two hours, though a relative of mine merely jogged it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For some' makes the definition fair: only the elite finish the 26.2-mile race in about two hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the elite finishing time identifies the long-distance road race.

clue.text: Maxim, a little saying, no meaning

indicators.note: only a little of the words is used, the part inside them

explanation.surface: Dismissing a proverb as a little saying with no real meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying, right beside Maxim, looks like the definition; the answer sits inside 'saying, no meaning'. The same word is an old term for an aphorism.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare sense: a short pithy saying, from Greek for opinion.

clue.text: Reportedly big jar

indicators.note: as reported, i.e. as heard spoken

explanation.surface: News of a large storage jar.
explanation.walkthrough: Jar looks like a pot; it is the verb, as in sounds that jar on the nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to have an irritating, rasping effect.
